rule: An atom that imports another tier is arranging children. It is a composite wearing the wrong name.
A behavior has no shape, so it has nothing to compose.
Stack imports Divider to place a rule BETWEEN children. The divider is the frame's own chrome, not content the caller passed. A frame never hand-rolls what an atom already owns.
A frame that reaches upward is reacting to content it must not know about.
The normal direction. A composite assembles atoms.
A composite arranges its atoms inside frames rather than hand-rolling flex.
A composite that knows a domain entity is a block.
Blocks reach every tier below them.
A page is a list of functions: which blocks, in which frames, fed which data.
A page reaching straight for an atom usually means a block is missing.
